## 46. Replaying the original local duality proofs

GCL has now compiled all 312 original modules in the import closure of the local duality entry module, using the original Lean v4.33.1 toolchain, compiler options and nine pinned dependency repositories. The official dependency cache was used, but none of the original submission's source or compiled proof artifacts was substituted. The final module `GcohTop` was separately replayed by Lean's kernel checker.

The declarations `Gcoh.top_locfin : LocalFinitenessK` and `Gcoh.top_tate : LocalTateDualityK` both have precisely three transitive axiom dependencies: propositional extensionality, classical choice and quotient soundness. The underlying `finite_cohomology_galois_top`, `subsingleton_cohomology_galois_top` and `localDualityHypotheses` declarations have the same axiom sets.

This distinction is important. A familiar theorem name is no evidence of a proof. The actual type, checked term, transitive assumptions, and mathematical interpretation must agree. Here the two local foundations have passed the original-source compilation and declaration-level checks; the global duality declaration still requires its own targeted replay.

The final local duality compiled artifact is byte-identical to both external builds. Of the 312 local artifacts, 280 match exactly; all 32 differences occur in warning-bearing modules, with an observed local source path inside a warning-bearing artifact. Selected differing artifacts passed kernel replay. This is consistent with diagnostic metadata differences, not a complete explanation of every differing byte.

## 45. What the independent kernel checks establish

The question of concealed assumptions is now supported by substantially stronger evidence. The [MIT verification dossier](https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/), updated 27 November 2026, reports a separate offline, read-only-source rebuild of the original 20 November archive and exact reproduction of its exported proof. The five canonical RH and Dirichlet GRH statements pass multiple independently implemented kernels and statement comparators. The [axiom audit](https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/audit.log) reports only propositional extensionality, classical choice and quotient soundness for the five headline theorems.

Think of the source as the construction instructions, the compiled declarations as the assembled parts, and the exported proof as a certificate that can be checked independently of the elaborator. Matching the final theorem against a canonical challenge prevents the certificate from proving a weaker replacement. Rebuilding the source in an isolated environment and obtaining the same certificate ties that certificate back to the actual submission.

GCL independently recomputed the original archive's digest, and reconciled its two foundational import closures against both external compilation manifests. All 312 local modules and all 1,915 global modules match across the two builds, comprising 1,925 distinct modules. All corresponding source hashes match members of the original archive. This is a module-specific comparison, not merely reliance on a headline assertion.

# CM5 R0: integer rank-one homology and stable finite generation (041)

## Disposition

The integral rank-one homology base is now kernel-checked.
The actual reduced Dold–Kan chain model of the integer group in
degree one has homology the integers in degree one and zero in
all other degrees. Every homology group of every positive-stage
rank-one Eilenberg–Mac Lane model is finitely generated. The actual
stable homology functor evaluated at the integer group is finite.

Parent PR #3853 merged at
1aef34aea4e3f3d8a8a133c825a369674a97e418.
This completes the rank-one finite-generation input for the
approximate-resolution induction in 016 and 030. It does not
construct LatticeBD.

## Equivariant integer-line comparison

Let V_n be the free integer module on (n+1)-tuples of integer
vertices. The simplicial vertex functor pulls back tuples along
ordinal maps; the actual alternating face differential deletes
vertices. Simultaneous translation commutes with the differential.
Prepending a chosen vertex a defines a cone c_a. For positive
degree its boundary identity is

$$
d c_a+c_a d=1.
$$

Translation carries this cone to the cone based at the translated
vertex. These statements are checked as maps, not just on a
chosen homology representative.

The two-term line resolution can be realized directly inside V,
avoiding the group-ring and representation-theoretic dependency.
The finite signed chain of unit edges P(a,b) from a to b is
defined by the coefficient at k of the step indicator at b
minus the step indicator at a. The support lies between a and b.
The following identities hold for arbitrary integers, including
negative endpoints and reversed paths:

$$
d P(a,b)=[b]-[a],\quad
P(a,b)+P(b,c)=P(a,c),\quad
T_s P(a,b)=P(a+s,b+s).
$$

# CM5 R0: finite homological models and the rank-one bar reduction (040)

## Disposition

The finite-free replacement and tensor-power finite-generation
mechanisms are now kernel-checked, as is induction over all positive
Eilenberg–Mac Lane stages from the actual additive bar base. This
does not assert the remaining rank-one bar homology computation.

Parent PR #3850 is protected at merge
60afab132850f9c6f09dcd3d522d9f2f88db1780.

## Finite subcomplex

Let C be any nonnegative integral chain complex with finitely
generated homology. For a finite submodule V contained in the range
of a linear map, choose finitely many generators of V and lift them.
The span of the lifts is finite and maps onto V.

In each degree choose a finite submodule of the cycles mapping
onto homology. Write L_n for its image in C_n. Define F_0=L_0.
Given F_n, the intersection of F_n with the range of the next
differential is finite by Noetherianity of finite integer modules.
Choose a finite lift U of this intersection into C_(n+1).
Put F_(n+1)=L_(n+1)+U. The exact equality is

$$
d(F_{n+1})=F_n\cap\mathrm{im}(d:C_{n+1}\to C_n).
$$

Thus these actual submodules form a complex. Its inclusion into C
is surjective on homology by the selected cycle representatives
and injective by the boundary-lifting equality. All degrees are
handled by one recursion, not by independent incompatible truncations.

If the original chain terms are free, the finite subcomplex terms
are finite and torsion-free, hence finite free over the integers.
Both complexes are bounded below and degreewise projective.
The Mathlib projective-complex quasi-isomorphism criterion supplies
a chain homotopy equivalence. This bypasses the infinite-rank
subgroup freeness/splitting step in the source reconstruction 030.
